title: Standard Rent Ceiling
text: A landlord cannot charge or receive rent in excess of the legally permitted 'standard rent' for premises to which the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 applies.

title: Restricted Grounds for Eviction
text: A landlord may seek possession of premises under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 only on specific grounds, including persistent non-payment of rent after due notice, unauthorised subletting or transfer of possession, unauthorised structural alterations, use of the premises in a manner causing nuisance or damage, bona fide personal occupation requirement, or where repairs/reconstruction necessitate vacant possession. Eviction without one of these grounds is not permitted for a tenancy the Act covers.

title: Landlord Repair Obligations
text: Landlords are responsible for major/structural repairs to the premises. If a landlord fails to carry out necessary repairs after being put on written notice, the Act permits a tenant to carry out those repairs and adjust reasonable costs, subject to the Act's procedure.

title: Security Deposit Practice
text: Unlike the Central Model Tenancy Act, the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 does not itself fix a single statutory cap on security deposits. Deposit amounts are typically governed by the specific agreement between landlord and tenant; a deposit that is a large multiple of monthly rent (e.g. beyond the 2-3 months customary in the Mumbai/Pune market) may warrant scrutiny even without a fixed statutory ceiling to cite.
source: Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 (no statutory deposit cap; customary market practice)
